title: A water board settles its swing weights

blocks.text: A water utility's board weighs three measures for its main renewals: breaks avoided, leakage avoided (megalitres) and operating savings ($k). Each has a reference swing, from no benefit to the amount in `REFERENCE`. The board follows the group procedure of swing weighting: every member writes down a private rating of each measure's swing against the biggest one, and the board then settles on the **middle** rating of its members for each measure (the median, which for an even number of members is halfway between the two middle ratings), so that one member at an extreme cannot drag the result.

Write `panel_weights(ratings)` in `panel.py`, where `ratings[measure]` lists the members' ratings, returning the weights. Then write `price(weights, reference, measure, base)`: how many units of `base` the weights say one unit of `measure` is worth, so the board can read its weights as prices ("one break avoided is worth $125k").
Work the first test's weights by hand before coding. About five lines.

cases.says: the members' ratings settle per measure and become weights that sum to 1, worked out by hand
the price of one unit of a measure, in units of the base measure, worked out by hand
one member's extreme rating does not move the settled rating
a panel with an even number of members settles halfway between the two middle ratings
